International Master's Program with Thesis
Head of the program: Dr. Alon Shepon
Program Coordinator: Lee Mori
Tel: 03-6406616
Written inquiries will be submitted and handled through the Inquiry Portal.
Each inquiry will be automatically routed to the relevant person handling the campus according to the subject, department, and applicant. You will also be able to see in the system the progress of all your inquiries on various subjects.
Using the system is simple and convenient, you can enter it from here or through the personal area using the "Inquiry Portal" button.
The duration of studies in the thesis track will be two years.
Based on the crucial understanding that the future of the environmental profession is both international and interdisciplinary, the curriculum has been designed to equip its participants with the broad knowledge and perspectives they need to meet the complex challenges that lie ahead.
Therefore, the courses cover basic scientific content necessary for understanding wide-ranging environmental problems, as well as general content related to the legal, ethical, physical and health issues related to sustainability and the environment. The Dept. of Environmental Studies at the Porter School of the Environment and Earth Science has long been recognized as one of Israel's most innovative environmental institutions, working to promote new areas of interdisciplinary environmental research, establish novel environmental teaching programs and strengthen the place of environmental issues on the academic and public agenda.
The M.A. program in Environmental Studies provides candidates with an intensive multidisciplinary insight into environmental studies with an emphasis on Israel's unique geographic and geopolitical setting.
A thesis track is an additional year to the Master’s non-thesis program. This option is available for outstanding students who would like to pursue an academic career and in-depth research. After completing the first year of core and elective courses in sustainability and environment, they will seek a mentor and pursue a thesis.
International Master's Program with Thesis (40-41 credit hours)
A successful completion of the program includes completing the following components:
1. Complementary course in statistics (not included in the number of hours for the degree).
2. Colloquium - Obligatory participation for two semesters during the degree - 1 credit.
3. Core courses - 18 credits
4. Elective courses - 12 credits
5. Seminars - 8 credits
6. Attending 10 Colloquium lectures related to your research topic over the course of the thesis year.
7. A course in research methods related to the thesis topic - 2-3 credits.
8. Submission of a full thesis and attendance in a thesis Final Exam (Thesis Defense).
Mandatory first aid course
All Graduate and Ph.D. students of the Faculty of Exact Sciences, must participate in First Aid training during the first year of their degree. It’s a 4 hours training that will take place on Friday by Magen David Adom. Exact details will be published a month before the training. No alternate dates will be offered during the year. The training will be held in English.
Please note:
1. Attendance in the First Aid training is mandatory during all sessions. Participants will be required to sign the attendance sheet during the training.
2. Students with a valid first aid certificate or who’ve served in the military as medics will be exempted by providing formal documentation.
The final grade for the degree is calculated according to the following:
Average of courses grades 40%
Thesis 45%
Thesis oral exam 15%
Deadlines
Students of the International MA in Environmental Studies program that are interested in the thesis track will submit an application according to the above requirements, no later than the end of Spring Semester of the first academic year.
Thesis Supervisors
Students are required to have two Thesis Supervisors, one of whom must be TAU tenured faculty. Attaining supervisors from different disciplines is encouraged in order to enrich the research and reflect inter-disciplinarity. There is a possibility of a single supervisor who is a senior faculty member of the Department of Environmental Studies. Finding supervisors is up to the student, but the Program may provide support and consultation. Any proposed supervisor who does not hold a tenure-track position at TAU must be first approved by the program's Academic Committee and then by TAU Vice Rector.
